name: What is the difference between Level 4 and Level 5 drywall finish?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Level 4 and Level 5 drywall finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Level 4 drywall finish typically involves taping joints and corners, followed by three coats of joint compound, leaving a smooth surface suitable for most flat paints or light textures. Imperfections might be visible under critical lighting. A Level 5 finish, considered the highest standard, includes all steps of Level 4 plus a thin skim coat of joint compound applied over the entire surface. This creates an exceptionally smooth, uniform surface, ideal for high-gloss paints, dark colors, or areas with critical lighting, minimizing any visible imperfections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Level 4 uses three coats of compound, suitable for most paints. Level 5 adds a full skim coat for a flawless, ultra-smooth surface, ideal for high-gloss paints.
